event_text: Battle of Nocera between Ranulf II of Alife and Roger II of Sicily.
headline: Norman Kingdoms Clash at Nocera
story: Barry gazed out at the armies assembled below, their armor glinting in the sunlight. 'Roger II of Sicily, Susan, attempting to expand his dominions into the mainland, while Ranulf II of Alife is having none of it.' Susan preened her feathers, eyeing the battle lines. 'Ranulf's managed to scrounge up some support from the local lords, but Roger's got the weight of the Norman kingdom behind him – not to mention a few choice mercenary units.' Barry snorted. 'And a talent for dramatic entrances, it seems. His knights are pouring onto the field like they own the place.' Susan watched with interest as the battle unfolded. 'The chroniclers will call this the Battle of Nocera, by the way. Ranulf's forces will put up a good fight, but ultimately, Roger's got the numbers and the expertise – he'll emerge victorious, having successfully asserted his claim to the Duchy of Apulia.'
regret_line: One wonders if Roger would've been quite so keen on conquest if he'd known it'd lead to a lifetime of bureaucratic tangles.
winner_line: The concept of feudal loyalty, which will continue to muddy the waters of medieval politics for centuries to come.
